summary: The client message selectors count a close the seat's host relayed, so when the host closes a reminder's winner the next one in its group becomes current, and the reminder winner is never mail the host closed (#4866, after db break-up step 4b-4)

replay.detail: No claim is written, read or replayed differently. A relayed close is kept in a member-local table that never replicates and is outside every digest.

schema.detail: A new member-local table, local_relayed_message_closes (message, host, receipt, closed_at_unix_ms, recorded_at_unix_ms), and an insert trigger that refolds the message's client selector header. Both are created at startup. There is no backfill: the table fills as reads hear closes.

rules.detail: When a seat's host answers a message view, list, fault target or wake read that its seat closed a message, the read queues the close and returns; it never waits for the writer. A background writer records at most 64 closes per transaction. The queue holds at most 256, and one past that is dropped until a later read hears it again. The selector header's closed column, and the open messages the non-paging client list picks a reminder's winner from, count a recorded close as they count one made here. A relayed close never feeds a revision, an updated_at, a message view's status or message_index. A client resource the host closed is history with reason closed, even when the host is silent at that read and its state shows this member's own records. Latency: a list shows the close one read after the read that heard it; that first read already leaves the closed message out of current mail, as before. The observation trim removes a relayed close once a close claim or closed mark here covers it, or once this member no longer holds the message.

compatibility.detail: No request, response or wire shape changes. A previous-release member never reads the table, so beside this build it lists as before. Marks are not on in any multi-member fleet yet, so nobody sees the gap this closes today.

downtime.detail: Creating the empty table and its trigger at startup takes no measurable time.

recovery.detail: Rolling back to an earlier build leaves the table and its trigger in place but inert, since the earlier build never writes the table. A header already folded closed by a relayed close stays closed until the next claim or mark of its message refolds it, at which point the earlier build counts only its own closes again. This fails safe: a message the host closed is never shown open because of it. Rolling forward again picks the kept closes back up at the next fold.
